holidays.name: National Apple Dumpling Day
holidays.description: A day for baking, buying, or devouring a whole apple wrapped in pastry, baked until golden, and often drowned in cinnamon syrup or cream. It lands just before autumn starts, which makes it a good excuse to start the cozy-dessert season.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. It has been celebrated each September 17 for years, timed to the fall apple harvest.
holidays.funFact: Apple dumplings go back centuries in European cooking. Early versions were often boiled in cloth, and the baked-in-pastry version later became a classic American fall dessert.

holidays.name: National Monte Cristo Day
holidays.description: A salute to the Monte Cristo, a sandwich of ham, turkey, and Swiss cheese. It is dipped in egg batter, fried until crisp, and usually dusted with powdered sugar and served with jam. It is a sweet-and-savory mashup, somewhere between a sandwich and French toast.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It honors the sandwich, which is a descendant of the French croque monsieur and became popular in the United States in the mid-20th century.
holidays.funFact: The sandwich is not named after the novel's hero. It is an American spin on the croque monsieur, and some restaurants serve it with raspberry jam.

holidays.name: Pet Bird Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the feathered roommates who whistle, squawk, and sometimes learn to imitate the microwave beep. Bird owners are invited to give their birds extra treats, fresh toys, and some attention.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. Pet bird fans have marked it on September 17 as a day to appreciate companion birds.
holidays.funFact: Parrots can live for decades. Some large species, such as macaws and cockatoos, can outlive their owners' other pets and sometimes even the owners themselves.
